newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: ING recommends reducing stake in Slovak.
newsitem.headline: ING recommends reducing stake in Slovak.

text.p: ING Barings, in a report to investors, recommends reducing stakes in Slovakia's sole shipbuilder Slovenske Lodenice a.s. (SLK) due to uncertainty over minority shareholder rights.
The report said it based its recommendation on a share price of 1,030 crowns. The share has been hovering below the 1,000-crown level for some time closing at 960 on Friday.
ING's Anna Bossong said she would maintain the recommendation but gave no price floor for the rating.
The report said the company's future profitability would hinge upon how successful its new majority shareholder, Chirana-Prema a.s., was in imposing stricter management controls.
"But it is not clear whether the new owner will respect the rights of minority shareholders, so we continue to rate the stock as reduce," the report said.
Chirana-Prema, Slovakia's largest medical equipment producer and exporter, and its subsidiary Chirana Export-Import a.s. took a stake of about 30 percent in SLK last August.
Chirana said investment in SLK was part of its long-term strategy and that it wanted to become a strategic partner with SLK in trade relations, especially regarding the export of cargo containers.

SLK's high net debt to equity ratio, 110.4 percent, and its 15-times ratio of equity value to earnings before interest, taxes and depreciation (EV/EBITDA) was also part of the reason to rate its shares as reduce, ING said.
SLK has a good underlying market position and the company has announced ambitious future plans, so that management control is viewed as crucial for the future prosperity of the company, ING said.
SLK said it expected a pre-tax profit of around 12 million crowns in 1996, compared to a 71.2 million crown gross in 1995.
It forecast 1997 gross profit at around 80 million crowns, producing 14 vessels for traditional Russian and German customers.
The investment plan for this year was set at 70 million crowns, which should be fully covered by own financial resources.
